description: Delney, Streetwise Lookout + Esper Sentinel: Esper Sentinel's 'draw unless opponent pays {X}' tax trigger is a power-1 creature's triggered ability, so Delney doubles it. Both independent instances offer the casting opponent their own pay-or-decline choice; this fixture demonstrates the 'decline both, can't afford either' branch (2 draws for the controller). Validates INT-0008.
artificial_state_elements: 3 Island for playerB were sized exactly to cast Divination ({2}{U}) with nothing spare, so both pay-{1}-or-decline choices are forced to 'can't afford it' regardless of the opponent's preference - this isolates the doubling mechanism from opponent-choice variance, not a claim that opponents always lack spare mana.
Divination was chosen as an arbitrary cheap noncreature spell; its own draw effect benefits playerB (the caster), not playerA, and is incidental to the interaction under test.
No other permanents, hand cards beyond what's listed, or players' boards were modeled.
material_characteristics: Esper Sentinel's power is exactly 1, so its own triggered ability qualifies for Delney's power-2-or-less doubling clause

Esper Sentinel's trigger is 'draw a card unless that player pays {X}' - a targeted-at-the-caster tax effect with an opponent-controlled pay/decline choice built in, distinct from Orcish Bowmasters' (INT-0007) any-target damage or Runic Armasaur's (INT-0009) controller-side 'may'

Delney's static ability produces two independently-resolved instances, each with its own pay-or-decline choice for the casting opponent (per the official Delney ruling on independent resolution-time choices)
abstracted_characteristics: Identity of the noncreature spell playerB cast (any noncreature spell triggers Esper Sentinel identically)
All board state not directly involved in the two-permanent interaction
The opponent's actual preference between paying and declining - this fixture forces 'decline' by removing the ability to pay, not by asserting opponents always decline

illegal_actions_to_reject: Any implicit assumption that Esper Sentinel's tax only fires once (Delney alone) rather than twice, each independently offering the pay-or-decline choice
Modeling the two instances as a single 'pay {2} total or draw 2' aggregate rather than two separate {1}-or-draw-1 decisions
expected.outcome_if_resolved: After seat 2 casts Divination and both Esper Sentinel trigger instances resolve (seat 2 unable to pay either {1}): seat 1's hand grows from 0 to 2 cards.

rules_citations: CR 603.2d (a triggered ability may be stated to trigger an additional time; determine how many times, then trigger that many times)
CR 603.3b (a player puts each of their own simultaneously-pending triggered abilities on the stack in any order they choose)
